memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"So Moses announced to the Israelites the appointed festivals of the
LORD" - Lev 23:44 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
One short verse closes the chapter. Moses announced them. He did not
edit the list, soften the hard parts or leave out the costly ones. He
passed on what God had given.

That is faithfulness in its simplest form.

Dear reader, it is tempting to hand on only the comfortable parts of
Scripture. We enjoy the verses about God's love and quietly skip the
ones about holiness, cost and self-denial. But a half-message produces a
half-formed faith.

Paul could tell the Ephesian elders that he had not hesitated to
proclaim to them the whole will of God (Acts 20:27). He told Timothy to
preach the word, in season and out of season (2 Tim 4:2) - meaning when
it is welcome and when it is not.

This applies to all of us, not only preachers. When you share your faith
with a friend, do you present a Jesus who asks nothing? When you teach
your children, do you give them a God who is only comfortable?

Look back over Leviticus 23. Rest and repentance. Feasting and fasting.
Celebration and solemn assembly. Generosity to the poor. Joy commanded
and sin acknowledged.

That is the whole picture. Receive it all, and pass it on faithfully.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do I share the whole of God's Word or only the comfortable parts?
2. What part of Scripture have I been quietly avoiding?
3. How has this chapter enlarged my picture of God?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Father, thank You for giving me Your whole Word. Give me courage to
receive all of it and faithfulness to pass it on without editing it.
Amen.
